svg.desc: Banner for a paper on when even-order Steiner distance hyperdeterminants of trees vanish. Title: Order six: zero for every tree with 350 edges. Subtitle: the published even-order theorem fails; the first counterexample is any tree on 351 vertices (Theorem 3.1). Left: the star with 350 leaves, a central hub joined to 350 leaves in three coloured groups: 288 leaves in blue, 31 in orange and 31 in pink. Middle: one number per link, from a list of three. 288 times 31 over 32 equals 279. 31 times (minus 9 plus 5 root 5) over 2 and 31 times (minus 9 minus 5 root 5) over 2 together equal minus 279. The sum is 0. Root 5 cancels only if the two 31s match; 31 and 288 share no factor, so 350 is the least. Right: whether every tree is nonzero, by even order k from 2 to 18. The theorem holds (green) at k = 2, 4, 8 and 12 and fails (orange) at k = 6, 10, 14, 16 and 18; the fewest vertices of a failing tree are 351 at k = 6, 6,805 at k = 10 and 684 at k = 16. It holds exactly when k minus 1 is 1 or a prime leaving remainder 3 on division by 4. Footer: exact contraction over all 351 to the fifth terms per vertex type; symmetric hyperdeterminant; unrefereed candidate.
